packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-14: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification of the work, author or a reading. The only identifying-type text seen is the modern pencil shelfmark on the parchment itself ("Stams, STA, Frg. 225-1r", "225-2r", "225-2v", "225-1v"), which names a holding, not a work. I did not search or consult anything; I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-018 in this packet (I probed image-019 by path to find the end of the series; it does not exist). I listed no directory.

IMAGES
- image-001: reduced overview, face A (two vertical parchment strips mounted side by side, pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 225-1r" under left strip, "Stams, STA, Frg. 225-2r" under right strip).
- image-002 to image-009: native tiles of face A (002 top-left, 003 top-right, 004 mid-left, 005 mid-right, 006 lower-left, 007 lower-right, 008 bottom-left, 009 bottom-right). They overlap; repeated lines are noted, not counted twice.
- image-010: reduced overview, face B (left strip labelled "225-2v", right strip "225-1v").
- image-011 to image-018: native tiles of face B (011 top-left, 012 top-right, 013 mid-left, 014 mid-right, 015 lower-left, 016 lower-right, 017 bottom-left, 018 bottom-right).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Portrait orientation. Two long narrow strips, each cut vertically; the cut between them is not a column gutter, so text runs into/out of the cut on each side. Both strips cut obliquely at the top corners; damage, tape repairs, a dark water/grime stain across the middle of both faces.
- Small Gothic textualis bookhand, brown ink, ruled, very dense abbreviation; about 55-60 lines survive per column on face A.
- Face A: left strip holds the right-hand part of one wide column (its left margin is blank parchment, so this is a column with outer margin at left); the right strip holds the continuation zone of a column, then a blank intercolumnar space, then the first 3-6 letters of the lines of a further column at the far right edge. Whether the right-strip main column is the same column as the left strip (i.e. the two strips joined across the cut) I cannot confirm: line heights look compatible but words do not bridge the cut cleanly in what I could read. Treat column order as uncertain.
- Face B: left strip has, at far left, line-endings of one column, then blank space, then a main column; right strip has a main column and wide blank margin at right.
- No rubrics or coloured initials visible. On face B there are short indented lines with underlining (image-011 lines 7-8; image-017 lines 6-7), which look like underlined lemmata/headwords set into the text; tentative interpretation: commentary with lemmata underlined. Many inline citations in the form ".j. de off. del.", ".j. de app.", ".j. de sen. ex.", "xi. q. iii.", "ii. q. vi.", "lxiii. d." (tentative: legal allegations). I make no inference about the work from this.
- Marginalia: face A, intercolumn of right strip, small note ":pañ" or ":pau" (image-007 line ~9 level); face A left strip, lower left margin, a faint short note in a different (reddish) ink, "aud[...]?" (image-006 lower left / image-008 line 4 level). Face B, left-strip margin: drawn pointing hand (manicule) with three short lines of tiny faint script below it (image-013, mid-lower margin), unread. Interlinear corrections/additions above words occur (e.g. superscript letters above "exhiberet", above "huius").

SELECTED SPANS / CONVENTIONS
Line numbers count from the top of each tile as visible text lines (partial lines at the very top edge counted as line 1). "..." at line start/end = text runs off the cut or tile edge. Expansions in parentheses, uncertain readings with "?", [illegible] where I could not read after looking.
Abbreviations: "ē" = est, "q" with stroke = quod/quia (given as q.), "⁊" = tironian et, "n̄" = non, "sn̄ia" = sententia.
